As much as we tease devs for clever use of resources, I think that kinda stuff needs to come back. In the older less hardware capable days, devs had to do stuff like... well, the example that immediately springs to mind is Fallout 3 Broken Steel, where rendering an actual metro train that moved realistically was too taxing with all of the other stuff in that cell. So they stuck their existing metro train model on top of the head of a naked NPC and had that NPC run along a set path. @GamersNexus  I am no naive about the business aspect of things. The GPUs I've owned range from 3DFX Voodoo 2 to Radeon HD5870 (yes I need to upgrade. Having been mostly non-gaming for a while It was not a problem, and these are hard times to find a good NEW mid-range GPU) passing by the first GeForce and a few others and I've been happy with all of them, so I can say I'm not biased.

The reason why I'm calling it foul play instead of regular business (by the way, I never said AMD never did it : still, 2 wrongs don't make one right) is because this RTX 30XX launch has been a complete, utter failure no matter how you look at it. And it doesn't matter that some people want to debate forever about the fact that it was an actual paperlaunch or not, just because a few units were actually sold : this is a rushed, weak launch.

Some people talk about this being business? Right. What I expect from such large companies is maturity. Having so few units, being so obsessive over what the other company is gonna do and having so few units to sell that no matter what measures sellers take, a large part of them will get scalped, is nothing like mature business to me.

Remember when you made fun of Intel introducing its new mobile CPUs and talking more about AMD than its own? Oh sure, Nvidia technically hasn't spelled AMD, but we all can hear it.

The most ironical part of it is that my current plan is to finally build my new RIG that will be used for both work and a few gaming, then "recycle" this one as a dedicated lab once DDR5 is out, (or the other way : after all, DDR5 will on the mid-term give us more RAM for less money, but I digress) and I REALLY wanted to get back to Nvidia because theorically these are very good products. Theorically is the word that hurts though : at this point, I'm going for what's actually available. Not saying RX 6X00 will have tons of stock (after all, people tend to forget that Zen 2 launch was... chaotic to say the least) but again, what bothers me from Nvidia this time is for them to try and draw so much attention on them while, with such a bad launch, all they should do is shut up and get actual available units as fast as possible.
